name: Sadya
desc: A vegetarian feast of up to 28 dishes on a banana leaf, eaten with the right hand. Served at Onam, weddings and some restaurants at lunchtime.

name: Appam with stew
desc: Lacy rice pancakes with a mild coconut-milk stew (vegetable, chicken or mutton).

name: Puttu and kadala curry
desc: Steamed rice and coconut cylinders with black-chickpea curry.

name: Idiyappam
desc: Steamed rice-noodle nests, usually with egg curry or stew.

name: Dosa and sambar
desc: Crisp fermented rice-lentil crepes with lentil-vegetable stew and chutneys.

name: Karimeen pollichathu
desc: Pearl-spot fish marinated in spices and roasted in a banana leaf. A backwater classic.

name: Alleppey fish curry
desc: Fish simmered in coconut milk with raw mango.

name: Fish moilee
desc: A mild, creamy coconut-milk fish curry with Portuguese influence.

name: Meen curry (red fish curry)
desc: Tangy and fiery, made with kudampuli (Malabar tamarind).

name: Kerala beef fry
desc: Slow-roasted beef with coconut slivers, curry leaves and black pepper.

name: Thalassery / Malabar biryani
desc: Fragrant short-grain kaima rice biryani from North Kerala, often with chicken.

name: Avial
desc: Mixed vegetables in coconut and yoghurt with coconut oil and curry leaves.

name: Thoran
desc: Dry stir-fry of finely chopped vegetables with grated coconut.

name: Pazham pori
desc: Ripe plantain fritters, the classic tea-time snack.

name: Banana chips
desc: Thin plantain chips fried in coconut oil. Good to take home.

name: Payasam
desc: Sweet milk or jaggery pudding that ends a Sadya.

name: Kozhikodan halwa
desc: Chewy, colourful halwa from Kozhikode's SM Street.
